member.name: T:JCass_Excel.LookupSheetEditor
member.summary:
Surgical editor for the value cell of (lookup_set_name, setting_key) rows in a Cassandra lookups.xlsx file. Patches column 3 of each matching row in-place and preserves any user content or formatting in adjacent columns (e.g. a "derivation" note in column D), which the bulk export-and-rewrite path in does not.
Sheets considered are those whose name begins with "lkp_" (case-insensitive). Header row is row 1 and is skipped during scanning.
The framework lookup loader reads cell values via Convert.ToString, so on the read path numeric and string cells are interchangeable. On the write path this editor parses each incoming value with : values that parse as a finite are written as numeric cells (so Excel does not flag "Number stored as text"), and values that don't parse are written verbatim as strings (e.g. enum keys, free-form notes).
Semantics: all-or-nothing. If any update's (set, key) is not found or is ambiguous (matches more than one row across all lkp_* sheets), no updates are applied and the file is not saved. The returned reports those problem keys for the caller to surface.

member.name: M:JCass_Excel.LookupSheetEditor.UpdateLookupValues(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{JCass_Excel.LookupUpdate})
member.summary:
Applies the given to the lookups.xlsx workbook at . Each update is keyed by composite (SetName, Key); column 3 of the matching row is overwritten with Value.
Returns an reporting the number of rows patched, plus any keys that were not found or were ambiguous. The file is saved only when every update resolves cleanly to exactly one row.

member.name: T:JCass_Excel.LookupUpdate
member.summary: One requested update: set column 3 of the row keyed by (SetName, Key) to . is always a string. Numeric strings are detected at the editor and stored as native numeric cells; format them with invariant culture (e.g. "1.25", never "1,25") so the parse succeeds regardless of the host machine's locale. Non-numeric strings (enum keys, free-form notes) are stored verbatim.
